attempts.bug_summary: When a standard dialect is configured with an explicitly supplied prefix, the returned configuration records the dialect's default prefix instead of the configured one. Processor registration still uses the explicit prefix, so the stored standard-dialect metadata can disagree with the processors that were actually aggregated.

Execution-attribute conflicts are checked against an entry's value rather than its name. As a result, dialects that define the same attribute under different values are incorrectly rejected in some cases, while duplicate attribute names can overwrite silently when their values do not happen to match an existing key.
